PRO SE INTERVENOR ROBERT FREEHILL’S
SUPPORT FOR PRO SE INTERVENOR JOHN B. BRADLEY III' S VERIFIED REQUEST FOR DISCLOSURE ON THE RECORD AND CONDITIONAL MOTION FOR RECUSAL OF CHAIRMAN THOMAS J. GLEESON

TO THE HONORABLE COMMISSIONERS OF THE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS:  Pro se Intervenor Robert Freehill, supports the filing by John B. Bradley, III, an intervenor appearing pro se, of the verified request for disclosure on the record and conditional motion for recusal of Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson, under 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 22.3(f)(1).

BACKGROUND
POLITICO published an article on 27OCT26, titled: “Texas officials huddled with tech companies before grid blitz”.  The article cites that on 16DEC25 [GOV] “Abbott’s top staff held a closed-door meeting on with representatives of the state’s largest tech and transmission companies”.  The article is Exhibit A in 59487 docket Item number 6670 and at Item number 6666.
According to the article, “the message from Abbott’s office was clear: We want data centers to come to Texas, and we want to work with the industry to remove roadblocks to make that happen.”
The article indicates that “Google, OpenAI, Meta, Amazon Web Services and Nvidia were “confirmed”” to attend this meeting as well as “the state’s four main electric transmission companies — Oncor Electric, CenterPoint Energy, AEP Texas and Texas-New Mexico Power.”.  It further identifies “PUC Chair Thomas Gleeson and his chief of staff as well as PUC deputy executive director Barksdale English. ERCOT CEO Pablo Vegas and three other top ERCOT officials, plus two consultants from McKinsey & Co., were also on the list.”  Note, also, that the attendee list does not appear to include any Landowners.

RELEVANCY
The Calendar titles this meeting a “Transmission Roundtable”
The reported attendee list included Chairman Gleeson, Chairman of the PUCT and representatives of Oncor Electric Delivery Company, an applicant in this proceeding.
This “Transmission Roundtable” occurred 6 months after the Salado, TX meeting I attended (16JUN25) and 3 months before the 26MAR26 filing of the Joint Application of ONCOR Electric Delivery Company, LLC and LCRA TSC to amend their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity for the BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT.

DISCUSSION
 From the documents obtained there is no indication of an agenda, discussion topics, meeting minutes or transcripts; however, this “Transmission Roundtable” was squarely within the project refinement window of the project.  Specifically, my initial notification in June of 2025 indicated that Segment F3 impacted my property.  In the actual STANDARD APPLICATION FOR A CERTIFICATE OF CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR A PROPOSED TRANSMISSION LINE that I received through the mail o/a 26MAR26, the Segment that impacted my property had been refined to Segment F34.  Did this “Transmission Roundtable” issue refinement guidance…were Courses of Action directed?  Given the information obtained to this point, we cannot discern the impact this “Transmission Roundtable” may have had on the project planning.  
Considering the Title/Topic, the attendees, and the timing, it is wholly reasonable to believe that the 765-kV Transmission Lines, including Import Path 2, among other considerations, could be discussed.  
Chairman Gleeson’s attending this “Transmission Roundtable” places into question the principle of impartiality.

STANDARD
IAW 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 22.3(f)(1), the Standards for Recusal of Commissioners, “[A] commissioner must recuse himself or herself from sitting in a proceeding, or from deciding one or more issues in a proceeding, in which any one or more of the following circumstances exist:  (1) the commissioner in fact lacks impartiality or the commissioner’s impartiality has been reasonably questioned.  

CONCLUSION
As such, I, Pro se Intervenor Robert Freehill, support the filing by John B. Bradley, III, an intervenor appearing pro se, of the verified request for disclosure on the record and conditional motion for recusal of Chairman Thomas J. Gleeson, under 16 Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 22.3(f)(1).
I further respectfully request the Commission to:
Grant pro se Intervenor Bradley's request for appropriate disclosure on the record concerning Chairman Gleeson's attendance and participation in the December 16,2025 meeting, including any discussions relevant to Import Path 2 or Docket No. 59475. And Docket No. 59182
Make available, to the extent authorized by law, relevant agendas, attendance records, communications, notes, and other records identifying the subjects discussed, guidance given and/or decisions made.
Determine whether any communications concerned disputed facts or legal issues relevant to the proposed transmission facilities and whether those communications implicate applicable ex parte or impartiality requirements.
Require Chairman Gleeson to recuse himself from further participation in Docket No. 59475, including deliberations and votes, if the established facts satisfy the recusal standard under 16 TAC § 22.3.
Permit pro se Intervenor Bradley to supplement his motion after receiving responsive public information records, consistent with applicable Commission procedures.

PRAYER
 I, pro se intervenor, Robert Freehill, do not allege that Chairman Gleeson is biased and ask for no finding of misconduct; I do reasonably question Chairman Gleeson's impartiality.  Impartiality is fundamental and is owed to all affected landowners and rate payer parties – this decision has enormous consequences.  Recusal IAW 16 TAC § 22.3(f)(1) is the only remedy to uphold the integrity of the Commission.
I, respectfully request that Chairman Gleeson grant the motion and issue his decision IAW 16 TAC § 22.3(g)(4).and recuse himself from deliberating or voting on whether to approve or deny the CCN applications in Docket Nos. 59182 and 59475, as well as any further deliberations and/or decisions regarding 59182 and/or 59475.

Respectfully submitted,
